ei.title: A Journey From War to the Olympics
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
When Yusra Mardini was a young girl growing up in Damascus, Syria, her life centered around swimming. Her father was a former professional swimmer, and she started learning how to swim from a young age. When she was nine years old, she was already faster than many older swimmers. It was clear that she had a special talent, and she fell in love with the sport. She enjoyed watching Olympic swimming events with her father, which led her to dream about competing in the Olympics. She got the chance to represent Syria in an international swimming championship, and it seemed like her Olympic dream might someday come true.

However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara. They realized that they could no longer stay in their home country, and they made up their minds to flee Syria and go to Germany to avoid the war. If they reached Europe, the rest of the family would follow. The decision was not an easy one, but Yusra knew that it was her only option if she wanted to pursue her dream and live without fear.

In August, 2015, the sisters began their dangerous journey by making their way to their first destination, Türkiye. There, along with 18 other people, including children and babies, they boarded a tiny boat designed for seven passengers. They were heading across the sea towards Greece when disaster struck. The boat's engine failed in the middle of the open sea, and the weather rapidly grew worse. The heavy boat began to sink, and the panicked, desperate passengers had no choice but to throw their possessions into the sea. Yusra felt heartbroken as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves. However, she had no time to reflect. She had to take action immediately in order to save herself and the other passengers. She jumped into the water along with Sara and two others, and the four of them guided the drifting boat. They swam for three and a half hours until they arrived safely with all the other passengers on the shore of a Greek island.

Next, Yusra and Sara had to travel through Macedonia, Serbia, Hungary, and Austria. They walked great distances, and even though they caught rides in small cars and crowded buses from time to time, they had to cross every border on foot. No matter how exhausted they were, they kept moving. At the end of this overwhelming 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a refugee center in Berlin. Despite all the hardships and adversities she underwent, Yusra's passion for swimming never left her. In fact, it was the only thing she could do to feel at home in this foreign land.

She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra stay focused and persistent in her efforts to pursue excellence. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would pay off one day.

Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro. Although it seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was hesitant. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might view her with pity instead of seeing her as a serious athlete. She almost turned down the invitation, but she decided to accept it after she realized that she could inspire hope in millions of other refugees facing similar challenges.

At the Games, Yusra competed in both the 100-meter butterfly and the 100-meter freestyle events. When she stepped onto the starting blocks, she was determined to pour everything she had into the competition. She came in 41st out of 45 competitors in the butterfly and 45th out of 46 in the freestyle event. Even though she left the Olympics without a medal, she was proud to have made history alongside her teammates. The time on the scoreboard did not matter. In one interview, when a reporter asked if she could make a statement, she remarked, "I want everyone to stay strong for their goals in life, because if you have your goals in front of your eyes, you will do everything you can; and I think even if I fail, I will try again. ... I want to show everybody that it's hard to arrive at your dreams, but it's not impossible. You can do it; everyone can do it."

questions.passage: When Yusra Mardini was a young girl growing up in Damascus, Syria, her life centered around swimming. Her father was a former professional swimmer, and she started learning how to swim from a young age. When she was nine years old, she was already faster than many older swimmers. It was clear that she had a special talent, and she ①<u>fell</u> in love with the sport. She enjoyed ③<u>watching</u> Olympic swimming events with her father, which ②<u>leading</u> her to dream about competing in the Olympics. She got the chance to ④<u>represent</u> Syria in an international swimming championship.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② leading → led: 주격 관계대명사 which의 동사 (과거시제)
det.analysis:
✅ ① fell: fall의 과거형. fell in love with 적절
❌ ② leading → led: which led her to dream. 관계대명사절 동사는 과거시제 ← 정답
✅ ③ watching: enjoyed + 동명사 적절
✅ ④ represent: to represent. to부정사 적절
det.tip: which + 동사: 선행사(events)가 아닌 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법. 시제 일치(과거) 필요.

questions.passage: In August, 2015, the sisters began their dangerous journey by making their way to their first destination, Türkiye. There, along with 18 other people, including children and babies, they boarded a tiny boat ②<u>designed</u> for seven passengers. They were heading across the sea towards Greece when disaster struck. The boat's engine failed in the middle of the open sea, and the weather rapidly ③<u>grew</u> worse. The heavy boat began to sink, and the panicked, desperate passengers had no choice but ①<u>throwing</u> their possessions into the sea. Yusra felt ④<u>heartbroken</u> as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① throwing → to throw: have no choice but to + 동사원형
det.analysis:
❌ ① throwing → to throw: have no choice but to V 구문 ← 정답
✅ ② designed: 과거분사. a boat designed for ~ 적절
✅ ③ grew: grow의 과거형. grew worse(더 나빠졌다) 적절
✅ ④ heartbroken: felt + 형용사보어 적절
det.tip: have no choice but to V = ~할 수밖에 없다. but 뒤에 to부정사.

questions.passage: She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin ①<u>who</u> could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her ②<u>swim</u>, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra ③<u>staying</u> focused and persistent in her efforts to pursue excellence. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, ④<u>hoping</u> her efforts would pay off one day.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ staying → stay: help + 목적어 + 동사원형
det.analysis:
✅ ① who: 관계대명사 주격. a coach who could help 적절
✅ ② swim: 지각동사 saw + 목적어 + 동사원형 적절
❌ ③ staying → stay: help + O + V(동사원형). helped Yusra stay ← 정답
✅ ④ hoping: 분사구문. ~하면서(동시동작) 적절
det.tip: help + 목적어 + (to) V: help는 목적격보어로 동사원형 또는 to부정사. 동명사 불가.

questions.passage: Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games. Although it seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was hesitant. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ faced → facing: 현재분사 (능동). 난민들이 도전에 '직면하고 있는'
det.analysis:
✅ ① joined: 가정법 과거. If she joined ~ might view 적절
✅ ② seeing: instead of + 동명사 적절
✅ ③ that: 명사절 접속사. realized that ~ 적절
❌ ④ faced → facing: refugees facing challenges. 난민들이 능동적으로 직면 중 ← 정답
det.tip: facing(현재분사): 주어(refugees)가 능동으로 직면하는 상황. faced는 과거분사(수동)로 부적절.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Yusra의 어머니는 전직 프로 수영 선수였다."

det.korean: F. 원문: 'Her father was a former professional swimmer.' 어머니가 아니라 아버지.
det.analysis:
❌ T: 어머니가 아닌 아버지가 전직 수영 선수
✅ F: father를 mother로 바꾼 오류 ← 정답
det.tip: father(아버지) ≠ mother(어머니). 세부 정보 변경에 주의.

questions.passage: In August, 2015, the sisters began their dangerous journey by making their way to their first destination, Türkiye. "Yusra 자매를 포함해 총 20명이 7인용 보트에 탑승했다."

det.korean: T. 원문: '18 other people'에 Yusra와 Sara를 더하면 20명. '7인용 보트(designed for seven passengers)'에 탑승.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 18명 + Yusra + Sara = 20명, 7인용 보트 맞음 ← 정답
❌ F: 계산이 맞음
det.tip: 18 other people + 자매 2명 = 총 20명. 수치 계산 문제.

questions.passage: At the Games, Yusra competed in both the 100-meter butterfly and the 100-meter freestyle events. questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Yusra는 접영에서 45명 중 45위를 기록했다."

det.korean: F. 원문: '41st out of 45 competitors in the butterfly.' 45위가 아니라 41위.
det.analysis:
❌ T: 접영 41위(45명 중)이지 45위가 아님
✅ F: 41st를 45th로 바꾼 오류 ← 정답
det.tip: butterfly(접영): 41st/45. freestyle(자유형): 45th/46. 수치 혼동 주의.

questions.passage: The heavy boat began to sink, and the panicked, desperate passengers had no choice but to throw their possessions into the sea. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 즉시 행동에 나서야(take action) 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② take action(행동에 나서다): 원문 일치. 물에 뛰어들어 보트를 이끌었음
❌ ① give up(포기하다): 즉시 행동한 것과 모순
❌ ③ call for help(도움 요청): 직접 물에 뛰어든 것
❌ ④ wait patiently(참을성 있게 기다리다): immediately와 모순
det.tip: take action = 행동에 나서다. 'jumped into the water'가 근거.

questions.passage: Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro. Although it seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was hesitant. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might view her with pity instead of seeing her as a serious athlete. She almost turned down the invitation, but she decided to accept it after she realized that she could ____ in millions of other refugees facing similar challenges.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 수백만 난민들에게 희망을 불어넣을(inspire hope) 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ inspire hope(희망을 불어넣다): 원문 일치. 수락 이유
❌ ① create fear(두려움 생성): 긍정적 결정과 모순
❌ ② cause confusion(혼란 야기): 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ provoke anger(분노 유발): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: inspire hope = 희망을 불어넣다. 'decided to accept it after she realized'가 단서.

questions.passage: However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 학교에 가는 것과 같은 평범한 활동이 위험해졌다

det.korean: ④ 원문: 'Although it did not explode.' 폭탄은 폭발하지 않았다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 2011년 내전: 원문 일치
❌ ② 평범한 활동 위험: 원문 일치
❌ ③ 혼란 속 수영 계속: 원문 일치
✅ ④ 폭탄이 폭발했다: 원문은 폭발하지 않았음 ← 정답(불일치)
det.tip: did not explode(폭발하지 않았다). not 부정어 주의.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Yusra의 수영에 대한 열정은 사라지지 않았다
독일에 도착한 후 Yusra는 수영을 포기했다

det.korean: ③ 원문: 'Yusra's passion for swimming never left her.'
det.analysis:
❌ ① 모든 국경 차량: 원문 'cross every border on foot'
❌ ② 15일: 원문 '25-day journey'
✅ ③ 열정 사라지지 않음: 원문 일치 ← 정답
❌ ④ 수영 포기: 원문과 정반대
det.tip: never left her = 그녀를 떠나지 않았다 = 사라지지 않았다.

questions.passage: ①She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. ②She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club far from the refugee center. ③When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to be her coach. ④Sven helped Yusra stay focused and persistent in her efforts to pursue excellence.
questions.stem: ①~④ 중 원문과 다른 부분을 포함하는 문장은?

det.korean: ② 원문: 'a swimming club near the refugee center.' → 'far from'은 오류.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 원문 일치
❌ ② far from → near: 난민센터에서 멀리가 아니라 가까이 ← 정답
✅ ③ 원문 일치
✅ ④ 원문 일치
det.tip: near(가까운) ↔ far from(먼). 원문 세부사항 변경.

In one interview, when a reporter asked if she could make a statement, she remarked, "I want everyone to stay strong for their goals in life, because if you have your goals in front of your eyes, you will do everything you can; and I think even if I fail, I will try again. ... I want to show everybody that it's hard to arrive at your dreams, but it's not impossible. You can do it; everyone can do it."
questions.stem: Yusra의 인터뷰 발언이 전달하고자 하는 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 올림픽에서 메달을 따는 것이 가장 중요하다
난민 선수들에게 더 많은 지원이 필요하다
목표를 향해 포기하지 않으면 꿈을 이룰 수 있다
실패 후 재도전하는 것은 시간 낭비이다

det.korean: 목표를 향해 포기하지 않으면 꿈을 이룰 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 메달 중요: 'The time on the scoreboard did not matter'과 모순
❌ ② 난민 지원: 인터뷰 내용에 없음
✅ ③ 목표 포기하지 않으면 꿈 실현: 'stay strong for their goals', 'it's not impossible' 직접 근거 ← 정답
❌ ④ 재도전 시간낭비: 'I will try again'과 모순
det.tip: 핵심 문장: 'it's hard to arrive at your dreams, but it's not impossible.'

✅ ① 전쟁 속 꿈: chaos 속에서도 clung to her dream. 글의 핵심 주제

det.korean: 독일(Germany).
det.analysis: ✅ Germany: 'flee Syria and go to Germany'에서 직접 확인.

다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바르게 배열하시오.

'그녀가 최대 잠재력에 도달하도록 도와줄 수 있는'

[ help / could / her / reach / who / full / her / potential ]
(8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'save(구하다)'인데, 'endanger(위험에 빠뜨리다)'로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① treasured(소중히 여기는): 원문 일치
✅ ② reflect(숙고하다): 원문 일치
❌ ③ endanger(위험에 빠뜨리다) → save(구하다): 자신과 승객을 '구하기' 위해 ← 정답
✅ ④ drifting(표류하는): 원문 일치
det.tip: save(구하다) ↔ endanger(위험에 빠뜨리다). 정반대 의미.

questions.passage:
She enjoyed watching Olympic swimming events with her father, which led her to dream about competing in the Olympics. She got the chance to ①<u>represent</u> Syria in an international swimming championship, and it seemed like her Olympic dream might someday come true.

However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned ②<u>upside down</u> by the horrors of the Syrian civil war. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she ③<u>abandoned</u> her dream and kept swimming. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a ④<u>wake-up call</u> for Yusra.

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'clung to(매달렸다)'인데, 'abandoned(포기했다)'로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① represent(대표하다): 원문 일치
✅ ② upside down(뒤집히다): 원문 일치

det.tip: clung to(매달리다) ↔ abandoned(포기하다). 꿈을 포기하지 않고 매달렸다.
